Now imagine coordinating thousands of actions across an entire software company.

That raises serious questions about reliability, persistent memory, hallucinations, prompt injection attacks, security, operating costs, and accountability.

In this video, we examine what Musk has actually announced, what independent reporting supports, and what remains speculation.

We also explore why Tesla shareholders are paying attention, how Macrohard compares with Microsoft's Copilot strategy and competing AI agents from Anthropic and Google, and what this could mean for developers, software companies, and businesses investing in AI automation.

Musk has access to enormous capital, AI research, custom Tesla chips, and computing infrastructure. But can those resources solve the reliability problems that still limit autonomous AI agents?

The real test isn't another announcement, acquisition, or ambitious prediction.

It's whether Macrohard can demonstrate a complete, useful workflow without a human stepping in to fix the mistakes.

Until then, is Macrohard the beginning of a fully autonomous software company, or a multibillion-dollar vision running ahead of the technology?

Hashimoto’s disease is the most common cause of hypothyroidism, accounting for around 90% of underactive thyroid cases.

Hashimoto’s is an autoimmune condition in which antibodies attack the thyroid gland. It’s very common, affecting roughly 1 in 10 people, and is far more common in women than men.

Many people with Hashimoto’s may not notice symptoms at first. Others may experience weight gain, dry hair, high cholesterol, fatigue, and difficulty sleeping.

In some cases, taking iodine may actually worsen symptoms. Many people with Hashimoto's who are taking synthetic thyroid hormones still struggle to feel better because the underlying autoimmune component is not being addressed.

Vitamin D plays an important role in thyroid health and function. Vitamin K2 and magnesium are important cofactors that support vitamin D function and absorption.

Most of the gluten people consume today comes from modern wheat, which contributes to inflammation and negatively affects thyroid health for many people. Genetic factors can also increase susceptibility to autoimmune conditions.

Selenium, zinc, and magnesium are essential trace minerals for a healthy thyroid and play a key role in converting T4 into the active thyroid hormone T3.

Modern wheat is also commonly sprayed with glyphosate. Although it’s considered “safe,” the long-term effects of this herbicide on thyroid health remain unclear.

Vitamin D can help support immune balance and reduce inflammation, which can be beneficial for people dealing with autoimmune disease.

videos.summary_source_text:
"I Nearly Walked Away From It All" | Dan Brown Reveals All Dan Brown joins George Harper Jr. on the Life on Tour podcast, presented by Buffalo Trace, at The Belfry ahead of the 2026 Husqvarna British Masters earlier this season. Dan reflects on his remarkable journey through professional golf, from coming close to walking away from the game in his early years as a professional to fulfilling his ambition of reaching the PGA Tour.

He opens up about the challenges and setbacks that threatened to derail his career, the determination it took to keep going, and his emotional victory in Munich following the loss of a close friend.

Chapters:
00:44 - Introduction
03:10 - Growing up in Yorkshire
06:10 - Representing England as an amateur
11:00 - Turning pro and early struggles
24:30 - Emotional win at the 2025 BMW International Open
30:30 - Honour tradition, embrace change

55:20 - The hard thing about golf

videos.title: Hur bygger vi nästa kapitel för svensk och europeisk industri?
videos.summary_source_text:
Hur bygger vi nästa kapitel för svensk och europeisk industri? Industrin befinner sig i ett skifte där fysisk AI, robotik och autonoma system skapar nya möjligheter att effektivisera arbetet och minska den fysiska belastningen i produktionen. Samtidigt handlar omställningen inte bara om vilken teknik vi kan införa, utan hur vi får människor och teknik att utvecklas tillsammans.
 
Det var ett av perspektiven som stod i centrum när några av Europas ledande industriföretag, entreprenörer och investerare samlades på Industrial Future Summit 2026, arrangerat av Combient Foundry.
 
🎥 Hör Jens Fath, Physical Product Development & Manufacturing på PwC Germany berätta om potentialen med fysisk AI i industrin och varför nästa steg inte bara handlar om tekniken, utan om att skapa rätt förutsättningar för människor att använda den. videos.title: 19.11.26 - RIFT Presentation
videos.summary_source_text:
19.11.26 - RIFT Presentation RIFT is a modern, non-custodial trading and financial technology ecosystem designed to bring together market access, education, intelligent execution, portfolio participation and professional trading infrastructure in one connected environment.

Built for both newcomers and experienced market participants, RIFT provides a structured journey from learning and practice through to increasingly sophisticated forms of market participation.

ONE ECOSYSTEM. MULTIPLE WAYS TO PARTICIPATE.

RIFT gives users access to a range of trading and financial tools, including:

• Demo Trading — Practice market participation using virtual capital while learning how markets, execution and platform functionality work.

• Spot Trading — Participate directly in spot markets while developing an understanding of market behaviour, patience and risk management.

• Futures Trading — Access leveraged markets with tools and functionality designed for more advanced trading strategies and risk management.

• Smart Money — Explore structured portfolio participation through features including mirror wallets and trading books, allowing users to move beyond focusing only on individual trades.

• Auto Trading Engine — Access structured automated execution through different environments designed to support systematic and repeatable participation.

• Prediction Markets — Participate in an emerging category of market infrastructure where users can trade contracts based on the probability of future events and outcomes.

• Prop Trading Infrastructure — Learn about and participate in the evolving world of proprietary trading, funded accounts, capital allocation, performance evaluation and professional risk management.

INTELLIGENT FINANCIAL INFRASTRUCTURE

RIFT is designed around the idea that the future of finance will combine human decision-making with intelligent technology.

Modern financial markets generate enormous amounts of information. Algorithms and AI systems can process data, identify patterns, monitor markets and support execution at a speed that is impossible for an individual human to replicate.

RIFT explores how these technologies can work alongside human judgement to create more structured and intelligent financial participation.

The objective is not simply to automate everything.

It is to combine people, data, technology, risk management and intelligent execution within a connected financial ecosystem.

EDUCATION AT THE CORE

RIFT places strong emphasis on education and developing a deeper understanding of financial markets.

Through the RIFT Before You Quit educational series, training sessions and community learning, participants explore subjects including:

• Trading psychology
• Risk management
• Capital preservation
• Portfolio construction
• Capital allocation
• Market structure
• Smart money concepts
• Futures and leverage
• Prediction markets
• Proprietary trading
• Behavioural finance
• Artificial intelligence
• Algorithmic execution
• Financial infrastructure
• Professional trading principles

The objective is to help participants understand not only how to participate in markets, but also why disciplined decision-making matters.

A STRUCTURED LEARNING JOURNEY

RIFT is designed to provide a progression from education and practice toward more advanced market participation:

Learn → Demo → Spot → Futures → Smart Money → Automated Execution → Professional Trading

Each stage introduces different concepts, technologies and levels of responsibility.

Rather than focusing solely on individual trades or short-term results, RIFT encourages participants to develop a broader understanding of risk, process, discipline and capital management.

NON-CUSTODIAL INFRASTRUCTURE

RIFT follows a non-custodial approach designed to give users greater control over their own funds and reduce the need to place assets into a centralized company-controlled account.

This reflects a broader movement within digital finance toward greater transparency, user control and blockchain-based infrastructure.

ACCESS FROM ANY DEVICE

RIFT is available through the web as well as its broader platform environment, making it accessible across modern computers, smartphones and other devices.

Its lightweight infrastructure is designed to make participation practical even for users with older devices, helping remove unnecessary technology barriers to accessing modern financial tools.

THE FUTURE OF FINANCIAL PARTICIPATION

Financial markets are changing rapidly.

Trading is becoming increasingly automated. Artificial intelligence is transforming data analysis. Prediction markets are creating new forms of information-based participation. Proprietary trading is expanding access to structured capital allocation models. Blockchain infrastructure is changing how digital assets can be held and transferred.

RIFT brings these developments together within one evolving ecosystem.

videos.title: BOUNCE-BACK: Colorado Avalanche DOMINATE Ducks as Wedgewood, Nelson and T.J. Hughes Impress
videos.summary_source_text:
BOUNCE-BACK: Colorado Avalanche DOMINATE Ducks as Wedgewood, Nelson and T.J. Hughes Impress Colorado Avalanche blank Anaheim Ducks behind Scott Wedgewood’s clutch shutout and an offensive surge led by Brock Nelson. Can the Avs maintain consistency and seize momentum with stars Cale Makar and Nathan MacKinnon sidelined?

Chris Micieli and Zach Pearson break down Colorado’s dominant 4-0 bounce-back win, spotlighting T.J. Hughes’ poise and playmaking, Devon Toews’ impressive offensive turnaround, and critical shifts in faceoff wins and special teams. The conversation explores key moments from Parker Kelly’s relentless forecheck to Adam Beckman’s physical debut, as well as the Avs’ defensive commitment against the Ducks’ top-ranked power play. Listeners get insights into the team’s resilience, evolving chemistry, and the puzzling up-and-down nature of recent performances.

Will this Avs squad finally find their groove with five days to reset, or are more rollercoaster nights ahead? Don’t miss the analysis and passionate fan reactions that sum up Colorado’s quest for consistency.

Isaiah J. Downing-Imagn Images

videos.title: Hindi - 19.11.26 - RIFT Presentation
videos.summary_source_text:
Hindi - 19.11.26 - RIFT Presentation RIFT is a modern, non-custodial trading and financial technology ecosystem designed to bring together market access, education, intelligent execution, portfolio participation and professional trading infrastructure in one connected environment.

Built for both newcomers and experienced market participants, RIFT provides a structured journey from learning and practice through to increasingly sophisticated forms of market participation.

ONE ECOSYSTEM. MULTIPLE WAYS TO PARTICIPATE.

RIFT gives users access to a range of trading and financial tools, including:

• Demo Trading — Practice market participation using virtual capital while learning how markets, execution and platform functionality work.

• Spot Trading — Participate directly in spot markets while developing an understanding of market behaviour, patience and risk management.

• Futures Trading — Access leveraged markets with tools and functionality designed for more advanced trading strategies and risk management.

• Smart Money — Explore structured portfolio participation through features including mirror wallets and trading books, allowing users to move beyond focusing only on individual trades.

• Auto Trading Engine — Access structured automated execution through different environments designed to support systematic and repeatable participation.

• Prediction Markets — Participate in an emerging category of market infrastructure where users can trade contracts based on the probability of future events and outcomes.

• Prop Trading Infrastructure — Learn about and participate in the evolving world of proprietary trading, funded accounts, capital allocation, performance evaluation and professional risk management.

INTELLIGENT FINANCIAL INFRASTRUCTURE

RIFT is designed around the idea that the future of finance will combine human decision-making with intelligent technology.

Modern financial markets generate enormous amounts of information. Algorithms and AI systems can process data, identify patterns, monitor markets and support execution at a speed that is impossible for an individual human to replicate.

RIFT explores how these technologies can work alongside human judgement to create more structured and intelligent financial participation.

The objective is not simply to automate everything.

It is to combine people, data, technology, risk management and intelligent execution within a connected financial ecosystem.

EDUCATION AT THE CORE

RIFT places strong emphasis on education and developing a deeper understanding of financial markets.

Through the RIFT Before You Quit educational series, training sessions and community learning, participants explore subjects including:

• Trading psychology
• Risk management
• Capital preservation
• Portfolio construction
• Capital allocation
• Market structure
• Smart money concepts
• Futures and leverage
• Prediction markets
• Proprietary trading
• Behavioural finance
• Artificial intelligence
• Algorithmic execution
• Financial infrastructure
• Professional trading principles

The objective is to help participants understand not only how to participate in markets, but also why disciplined decision-making matters.

A STRUCTURED LEARNING JOURNEY

RIFT is designed to provide a progression from education and practice toward more advanced market participation:

Learn → Demo → Spot → Futures → Smart Money → Automated Execution → Professional Trading

Each stage introduces different concepts, technologies and levels of responsibility.

Rather than focusing solely on individual trades or short-term results, RIFT encourages participants to develop a broader understanding of risk, process, discipline and capital management.

NON-CUSTODIAL INFRASTRUCTURE

RIFT follows a non-custodial approach designed to give users greater control over their own funds and reduce the need to place assets into a centralized company-controlled account.

This reflects a broader movement within digital finance toward greater transparency, user control and blockchain-based infrastructure.

ACCESS FROM ANY DEVICE

RIFT is available through the web as well as its broader platform environment, making it accessible across modern computers, smartphones and other devices.

Its lightweight infrastructure is designed to make participation practical even for users with older devices, helping remove unnecessary technology barriers to accessing modern financial tools.

THE FUTURE OF FINANCIAL PARTICIPATION

Financial markets are changing rapidly.

Trading is becoming increasingly automated. Artificial intelligence is transforming data analysis. Prediction markets are creating new forms of information-based participation. Proprietary trading is expanding access to structured capital allocation models. Blockchain infrastructure is changing how digital assets can be held and transferred.

RIFT brings these developments together within one evolving ecosystem.

Battery test between Linux (Fedora) and Windows 11 to see which one is more efficient in real-world apps and workflows. We used two identically configured Dell XPS 13s (Intel Core 5 320, 8 GB RAM, 512 GB SSD).

TEST NOTES:

- Screens were calibrated to 200 nits with auto brightness turned off.
- Speakers calibrated to the nearest decibel count.
- Tested within equal distance of a WiFi access point.
- Tested in a temperature-controlled environment.
- Both laptops were set to their respective Balanced power profiles.
- Results ending at “shutdown” were based on each operating system’s automatic behavior.
- On Fedora, we installed RPM Fusion’s full-codec Intel VA-API media driver, adding hardware-accelerated H.264 and HEVC support omitted from Fedora’s stock driver.
- Fedora’s speaker-amplifier configuration was manually corrected because the XPS 13’s amplifiers were not properly enabled out of the box.
- Minecraft was capped to 30 FPS. Both laptops were able to well exceed this, but we kept it low to guarantee a performance match. 
- The tests used two identically configured but physically separate laptops. Small differences in battery capacity, silicon quality, cooling, or manufacturing could affect the results.

videos.summary_source_text:
We Asked 4,000 Golfers Which Premium Ball They Play. It’s Closer Than You Think Which premium golf ball are golfers actually playing? More than 4,000 MyGolfSpy readers answered our 2026 Golf Ball Survey, and 3,119 of them play a urethane-cover ball. The Titleist Pro V1 leads at 13.0%, but the Maxfli Tour X is only 0.8 points behind at 12.2%. Titleist has more players overall, but Maxfli's strength is concentrated in one ball. And the fifth most-played urethane ball isn't even made by a golf company.

These results reflect MyGolfSpy survey respondents, not all golfers.

Which golf ball are you playing right now? Tell us in the comments.

Google just surprise-dropped Gemini 4 Neon, beating Claude Opus 5.5 and GPT-6.2 Sol on major benchmarks while costing less than half as much as Claude on a real coding test. Meanwhile, Google researchers reveal AI that remembers how to improve itself across different models. Microsoft uses Claude to build working neural networks from just 166 parameters without training, while launching faster, cheaper AI models powered by Google's Gemma 4. Kling Image 4.0 brings native 8K generation, and HeyGen Avatar 6 becomes so realistic that testers mistake AI-generated footage for real video 42.2% of the time.

PGA Tour Highlights | Round 1 | The RSM Classic | 2026 Check out the best shots of the day from Round 1 of the 2026 The RSM Classic, featuring Max Greyserman, Michael Thorbjornsen and Jackson Koivun, among others.

The PGA Tour season reaches its conclusion this week at The RSM Classic, with plenty at stake at Sea Island as players make their final push for 2027 status. Only the top 100 in the FedExCup Fall standings will secure full playing privileges, leaving several notable names under pressure. Billy Horschel sits just outside the line at No. 101, while Joel Dahmen, Luke Clanton and Haotong Li face a steep climb from further back. Peter Malnati has an even tougher task at No. 151, knowing only a victory can take him into the top 100. Sami Valimaki returns to defend his title, while five-time major champion Brooks Koepka makes his tournament debut. The Aon Next 10 is also up for grabs, with places 51-60 earning starts in the first two Signature Events of 2027. The lineup also includes the in-form Andrew Novak, Austin Smotherman and Blades Brown as well as Major Champion Brian Harman, the field is stacked and it is set to be a thrilling finale.

videos.title: How to Become Rich in Ways You Never Imagined | Dr. Mandell
videos.summary_source_text: How to Become Rich in Ways You Never Imagined | Dr. Mandell What if everything you thought you knew about being rich was wrong? We spend so much of our lives chasing money, success, and possessions, believing that one day they will bring us true happiness. But the greatest riches in life cannot be bought, borrowed, or replaced. True wealth is found in the love we share, the family and friends who stand beside us, the health we often take for granted, the memories we create, and the precious moments that make life meaningful. Sometimes we become so focused on what we don't have that we forget how blessed we already are. In this heartfelt and inspiring message, Dr. Alan Mandell reminds us that the richest people aren't necessarily those who have the most money, but those who recognize the priceless gifts already surrounding them. Take a moment to reflect, appreciate the people you love, and remember that time is one treasure we can never get back. If this message touches your heart, share it with someone you love. videos.title: Gemini 4 Neon Is Here: Google’s Powerful Model Just Beat GPT-6.2 Astra!
videos.summary_source_text:
Gemini 4 Neon Is Here: Google’s Powerful Model Just Beat GPT-6.2 Astra! Google just released Gemini 4 Neon, only six days after Gemini 4 Hydrogen. Independent benchmarks place it among the world's most intelligent AI models, delivering nearly twice Carbon's output speed at a significantly lower cost per task. But one sentence buried inside Google's model card changes how you should look at this release.

Gemini 4 Neon is officially described as "adapted from Gemini 4 Carbon." No disclosed new architecture, no parameter count, and no confirmed training breakthrough. So is Neon genuinely a next-generation AI model, or an exceptionally well-optimized version of Carbon?

Google has now released four Gemini 4 models in just seven weeks: Argon, Carbon, Hydrogen, and Neon. The latest release also arrived just one day after OpenAI introduced GPT-6.2 Astra and Sol into its API.

In this video, we break down Gemini 4 Neon's independent benchmarks, real-world capabilities, reasoning performance, pricing, spectacular launch demos, technical limitations, and the important details Google buried in its benchmark footnotes.

Artificial Analysis ranked Gemini 4 Neon third overall on its Intelligence Index at its highest reasoning setting, behind GPT-6.2 Astra and Claude Fable 5.2. Neon scored 61 compared to Carbon's 60, while delivering approximately 110 tokens per second against Carbon's 57.

Vals AI also ranked Neon second out of 42 models, with particularly strong performance in finance and legal tasks. Independent evaluations suggest that Google's biggest achievement isn't necessarily higher intelligence — it's making near-frontier intelligence faster and cheaper.

But Google's own benchmarks deserve closer examination.

On SWE-sweep, Neon achieved an impressive 39.0 using Google's Antigravity CLI, compared to Claude Opus 5.5's 10.1 and GPT-6.2 Sol's 8.3. Switch to a neutral testing harness, however, and the competitive advantage changes dramatically. We examine why agent infrastructure, subagents, tool access, and execution environments matter just as much as the underlying model.

Then there are Google's spectacular demonstrations:

- A realistic Mont Blanc skiing simulator with approximately 10,200 lines of custom shader code.
- A spreadsheet-based photo editor using roughly 100,000 cells and over 500,000 formulas.
- A reconstruction of Alan Turing's 1936 study with a working Universal Turing Machine.
- A Blender-generated laboratory environment using MCP integration.
- A multi-agent game built using Antigravity's /swarm command.

These demonstrations showcase impressive coding, planning, and tool orchestration capabilities. However, they haven't been independently reproduced, and Neon itself remains a text-output model rather than a native 3D generator.

We also investigate why Neon's highest thinking level isn't necessarily its best. Going from high to xhigh reasoning delivers only one additional Intelligence Index point while adding nearly seven minutes of average task time. On one visual benchmark, performance actually declines.

Gemini 4 Neon supports a massive 1,048,576-token context window, multimodal inputs, up to 3,000 images, 3,000-page documents, and approximately 8.4 hours of audio. But documented capacity and demonstrated reliability are two very different things.

At $3 per million input tokens and $15 per million output tokens, Neon sits between GPT-6.2 Sol and Claude Opus 5.5 in standard API pricing, while remaining significantly cheaper than GPT-6.2 Astra and Claude Fable 5.2.

We break down the hidden costs of thinking tokens, context caching, search grounding, Antigravity's context limitations, and the difference between price per token and price per completed task.

Perhaps the biggest unanswered question, however, is safety.

Google has not yet published Neon's full Safety and Security Report. Some evaluations were inherited from Gemini 4 Argon, while hallucinations, jailbreak resistance, prompt injection, and agent security remain important considerations for developers and enterprises.

Is Gemini 4 Neon the best practical AI model for developers, coding agents, automation builders, and professional workloads? Or are Google, OpenAI, and Anthropic increasingly competing through efficiency and agent infrastructure rather than fundamental intelligence breakthroughs?

Watch the full breakdown before deciding which AI model deserves your money.

videos.summary_source_text:
How to Target Your Lower Abs (GET A FLATTER STOMACH) Get a flat stomach here - https://athleanx.com/flatstomach  
Subscribe to this channel here - http://bit.ly/2b0coMW

If you want more visible lower abs, pay attention to what happens *after* you bring your knees up. Can you curl your pelvis toward your chest, or do your legs move while your tailbone stays on the floor? That last part of the rep is easy to miss, and it can change how much work your abs actually do. In this video, I’m going to show you three lower ab exercises you can do at home, plus a bonus exercise for the pull-up bar. I’ll also cover where nutrition comes in if lower belly fat is hiding the muscle you’re working to build.

Can you target your lower abs? Your upper and lower abs are part of the same muscle, so both contribute when you do a crunch or a reverse crunch. You can, however, change the emphasis by changing which end of the movement you initiate from. In a standard crunch, you lift your shoulder blades off the floor and bring your rib cage toward your pelvis. To put more emphasis on the lower abs, work from the bottom up and bring your pelvis toward your rib cage.

You can feel the difference before you even start your first set. Lie on your back with your hips and knees bent to about 90 degrees. Now tip your belt buckle toward your chest until the gap underneath your low back closes. That’s a posterior pelvic tilt. From here, see if you can lift your tailbone an inch off the floor while keeping the bend in your hips and knees. It’s a small movement, but it’s the one I want you to recognize in each of the exercises that follows.

You can use that same setup to adjust the difficulty. Bring your thighs a little closer to your chest for an easier rep, or start with them farther away to make it harder. Once you pick an angle, hold it as you curl up. If your knees travel several inches before your tailbone starts to move, bring your thighs a little closer and try again.

First up are swipers. Start on your back with your legs raised and your hands beside your hips. Curl your pelvis up until you have enough room to swipe your hands together underneath your butt. What I like about this lower ab exercise is that every rep gives you feedback. If your feet went higher but your hands still hit the floor on either side of your hips, you know exactly what was missing. Reset, tuck your pelvis and lift again.

Next is the reverse knee tuck, an exercise I’d actually call a tailbone lift. Tell someone to tuck their knees and they can pull them all the way toward their abdomen while their pelvis barely moves. On your next rep, keep the bend in your knees and think about peeling your tailbone off the ground. Your knees will travel toward forehead level as your hips roll up. Lower yourself slowly enough to feel your pelvis return to the floor before you start the next rep.

The third exercise is the plank knee slide. This is where you take that same pelvic curl and use it in a plank. As you draw one knee forward, tuck your pelvis underneath you. It’s easy to rush through these and turn them into mountain climbers, so take your time on the way in and on the way back. If your low back sags as you extend your leg, reset your plank before you switch sides.

For a bonus, grab a pull-up bar and try the hanging leg raise. Here’s my favorite cue for this one. Imagine you’re trying to show your butt to the person standing in front of you. You can raise your thighs to waist height and still have your belt buckle pointing straight ahead. Curl your pelvis forward and watch where that belt buckle goes. Your hip flexors help lift your legs, and your abs do the work of curling your pelvis up against gravity. Control the descent so you can start the next rep without swinging.

Want to make these lower ab exercises harder? On swipers, reverse knee tucks and hanging leg raises, cross your legs and squeeze them together to engage your inner thighs. On plank knee slides, press your planted foot into the floor and imagine dragging it inward without letting it move. You can also add a small amount of rotation by curling one side of your pelvis toward the opposite side of your rib cage.

What about losing lower belly fat? These exercises can strengthen your lower abs, but you can’t choose where you lose fat by choosing which ab exercise you do. If your goal is a more visible six pack, your nutrition needs to support overall fat loss. That means maintaining a calorie deficit over time while you continue to train.

videos.summary_source_text:
Omöjligt uppdrag på stekhäll #350 I Kapten Mat Kaptenens gourmethelg på Wisingsö Hotell bokar du här: 
https://boka.wisingso.se/package/package-details?channelid=dae7aa86-a151-492a-9b7d-38a6c2e046e5&packageid=9690cf56-227b-44db-ad2a-e7fb3f7bdffd

Skånsk äggakaka med rökt sidfläsk och lingonsylt
6 portioner · ca 50 min

ÄGGAKAKAN
10 ägg
3,5 dl vetemjöl
2 tsk salt
1 l mjölk
75 g smör

FLÄSKET
400–800 g rökt sidfläsk i ca 1 cm tjocka skivor

LINGONSYLTEN
225 g lingon, färska eller frysta
1,25 dl strösocker (ca 110 g)
0,5 dl vatten
4 cl eau-de-vie

GÖR SÅ HÄR:
Lingonsylten: Koka upp lingon och vatten i en kastrull. Rör ner sockret och låt sylten sjuda på medelvärme i ca 8–10 min. Rör om då och då. Skumma av ytan och dra kastrullen från värmen. Rör ner eau-de-vien och låt sylten svalna. Den tjocknar när den kallnar.

Smeten: Börja med att vispa äggen. Vispa sedan i mjöl och salt. Vispa i hälften av mjölken och sedan resten. Låt smeten vila i en kvart.

Fläsket: Stek fläsket på medelvärme i stekhällen tills det är knaprigt. Lyft upp det och håll det varmt. Låt allt flott ligga kvar i hällen och lägg i smöret och låt det smälta.

Stek första sidan: Rör om smeten och häll den i hällen. Sänk till låg värme. Skrapa med spackelspaden från kanterna in mot mitten. Låt kakan stelna utan lock i ca 15–20 min samtidigt som du skrapar. Kanterna ska släppa och ytan nästan ha stelnat.

Vänd: När kakan har stelnat vänder du den med hjälp av en pizzaspade.
Stek klart under lock i ytterligare 5-10 min.

Servera: Lägg tillbaka fläsket ovanpå äggakakan och servera direkt från hällen med lingonsylten.

TIPS:
Låg värme är det viktigaste. Är värmen för hög blir botten bränd innan kakan har stelnat.
Gör gärna lingonsylten dagen innan. Den håller ca 2 veckor i kylen.
Sylten innehåller alkohol, ca 4–5 vol% med en eau-de-vie på 40 %. Hoppa över eau-de-vien om barn ska äta, eller koka med den i några minuter så att en del av alkoholen kokar bort.
Bärhalten i den färdiga sylten är ca 55–58 %.
I glaset: kall mjölk, en lager eller ett skånskt öl.

Vänd: När kakan har stelnat vänder du den med hjälp av en pizzaspade.
Stek klart under lock i ytterligare 5-10 min.

Servera: Lägg tillbaka fläsket ovanpå äggakakan och servera direkt från hällen med lingonsylten.

TIPS:
Låg värme är det viktigaste. Är värmen för hög blir botten bränd innan kakan har stelnat.
Gör gärna lingonsylten dagen innan. Den håller ca 2 veckor i kylen.
Sylten innehåller alkohol, ca 4–5 vol% med en eau-de-vie på 40 %. Hoppa över eau-de-vien om barn ska äta, eller koka med den i några minuter så att en del av alkoholen kokar bort.
Bärhalten i den färdiga sylten är ca 55–58 %.
I glaset: kall mjölk, en lager eller ett skånskt öl.

Kaptenens kökshandduk från Ekelunds Linneväveri handlar du här:
https://kaptenmat.se/produkt/handduk-kapten-mat-ekelund/

Min kokbok handlar du hos din bokhandlare eller direkt i min webbshop:
https://kaptenmat.se/produkt/kokbok-vara-mest-alskade-matklassiker/

Rör ner sockret och låt sylten sjuda på medelvärme i ca 8–10 min.

Did this Luxury Chinese SUV just KILL the UK car industry? Is a £57,000 Chinese SUV more luxurious than a £200,000 Range Rover SV?! 

Get 20% off CarVertical using code Carwow: https://www.carvertical.com/carwow 

Introducing the Li Auto L9 Livis! It’s an all-new luxurious SUV that is set to go on sale in the UK next year. 

It’s packed full of tech and luxurious features, and it clearly has class leaders such as the Range Rover in its sights! The question is, does it have what it takes to go toe-to-toe with a brand as renowned as Range Rover? 

To find out, Mat’s brought the two of them together to see just how they compare. So let’s take a closer look at the L9, starting with the design! 

Up top, the first thing you’ll notice is the huge swooping DRL that runs across the front of the car. Below this sit a pair of matrix LED headlights, and there are panels in the centre of the bumper that open up to assist with airflow. Along the side, the two-tone paint job helps give the car more presence, and there are a host of cameras and sensors on the car to assist with autonomous driving and parking. The side view also highlights just how big the car is, stretching to 5.2m long! Around the back, there’s a taillight that stretches across the length of the car, but otherwise it’s a relatively plain rear end. 

While the exterior may have been relatively plain, the interior comes absolutely packed with features. At the front, there’s a huge infotainment screen stretching across the length of the dash, and there’s Nappa leather on the steering wheel and seats. In fact, every surface you touch in the front is covered in soft-touch materials! 

The L9 is a six-seater, so step into the back, and you’ll find a pair of Captain’s chairs! They’re full of adjustments and massage functions, and there’s a retractable touchscreen that drops down from the roof, similar to what you’ll find in a BMW 7 Series. There’s also a fridge, blinds for the windows, and the third row of seats also comes with the ability to recline. There’s no denying it’s one luxurious interior! 

Under the bonnet? Well, in comparison to the Range Rover’s V8, here you’ll only find a 1.5-litre turbo petrol. However, this isn’t the L9’s main power source - it’s used as a generator to power two electric motors, and these combine to produce 571hp and 710Nm! 

The L9 Livis only costs around £57,000 in China, so it’s around a quarter of the price of the Range Rover SV! The question is, if you’re in the market for a luxurious SUV, would you be willing to choose a new Chinese entrant over an established brand like Range Rover? Let us know in the comments!

videos.title: 18.11.26 - Ep.26 (Part 8) - CLOB vs AMM
videos.summary_source_text:
18.11.26 - Ep.26 (Part 8) - CLOB vs AMM In this session, we continue our exploration of modern market structure by comparing Central Limit Order Books (CLOB) with Automated Market Makers (AMMs). Although both systems provide ways to trade the same assets, the way liquidity is organised, prices are determined and trades are executed can be fundamentally different.

We examine how these two models operate, why liquidity depth matters, and how execution quality can be affected by the structure of the market. We then move deeper into decentralised finance, exploring on-chain transaction ordering, Maximum Extractable Value (MEV), sandwich attacks, slippage tolerance and the network costs that traders need to consider before executing a trade.

The session also connects these concepts to RIFT’s trading environment, explaining why understanding both traditional order books and DeFi liquidity pools is important for anyone developing into a professional trader.

Topics Covered

CLOB vs AMM Architecture – How individual buy and sell orders provide liquidity in an order book, compared with liquidity being supplied collectively through an AMM pool.

How Prices Are Determined – The role of buyer and seller competition in CLOB markets, compared with pool reserves, mathematical pricing curves and liquidity ranges in AMMs.

Liquidity Depth and Large Orders – How large orders move through an order book in stages, while AMM trades move along a pricing curve, creating price impact depending on the size and depth of the pool.

Liquidity Providers and Market Makers – The different roles played by limit-order participants, market makers and AMM liquidity providers.

Price Alignment and Arbitrage – How trading activity and arbitrage help keep prices aligned across different exchanges and liquidity pools.

On-Chain Order Books – How Hyperliquid combines on-chain infrastructure and blockchain settlement with a traditional-style order book and price-time priority.

Understanding Hybrid Market Structure – Why the distinction between centralised and decentralised trading is no longer simply a distinction between order books and AMMs.

Transaction Ordering and MEV – How pending blockchain transactions can be observed and reordered, and why transaction priority can have economic value.

Sandwich Attacks – How automated searchers can front-run a pending swap, allow the user's transaction to execute at a worse price, and then back-run the trade to capture a profit.

Slippage Tolerance – How traders set acceptable execution boundaries, and the trade-off between protecting against poor execution and increasing the likelihood of a transaction failing.

On-Chain Trading Costs – Why network, swap and routing fees matter, particularly when executing smaller trades or using complex transaction routes.

Liquidity Aggregation and Smart Routing – How systems can split larger trades across multiple pools and decentralised exchanges to find better combinations of available liquidity.

Transparency vs Complexity – Why visible blockchain data does not automatically make market activity easy to interpret or guarantee better trading decisions.

The Trader's Execution Checklist – The key questions to ask before trading, including liquidity depth, spread, queue position, price impact, fees, slippage limits and network conditions.

What You Will Learn

By the end of this session, you should have a clearer understanding of how order-book and AMM markets differ, how decentralised trading introduces additional execution risks, and why the quality of a trade depends on more than simply choosing the right direction.

Whether you are trading through an order book or interacting with DeFi liquidity pools, understanding the market structure behind your trade is essential.

videos.title: Every Shot of Rory McIlroy's Final Round | 2026 DP World Tour Championship
videos.summary_source_text:
Every Shot of Rory McIlroy's Final Round | 2026 DP World Tour Championship Every shot of Rory McIlroy's final round of the 2026 DP World Tour Championship where he tried to go on and claim his EIGHTH Race to Dubai title.

► SUBSCRIBE: http://et.golf/Subscribe 

After visiting 25 countries across five continents, the DP World Tour’s schedule reaches a climax this week in Dubai, for the DP World Tour Championship, marking the final event of the 2026 Race to Dubai season. Since 2009, the DP World Tour Championship has annually played host to the season-ending event. Contested over 72 holes, with no cut, the final Rolex Series event features a $10 million prize fund, the biggest of the 2026 Race to Dubai season. 50 players have made their way to the second of back-to-back Rolex Series events, which form the DP World Tour Play-offs. There are two key pieces of silverware on offer this week, The DP World Tour Championship and the Harry Vardon Trophy. The battle for the Race to Dubai title comes to an end this week at Jumeirah Golf Club as players vie to end the year as DP World Tour Number One. There are still nine players in the running to end the year at the top of the Ranking. Eugenio Chacarra, the only three time winner this season, tops the standings heading in with a 533.93 point lead over nearest challenger Rory McIlroy, who is seeking to match Colin Montgomerie’s long-standing record of eight Order of Merit titles this week. With Patrick Reed, Casey Jarvis, US PGA Championship winner Aaron Rai, Jon Rahm, Ryan Fox, Jayden Schaper and Daniel Hillier all are still in with a chance of ending the year as the winner of the season-long race.

Avalanche Struggle To Find Offense in Loss to Utah. Winter Classic Uniforms Revealed. Colorado Avalanche struggle offensively as injuries to Cale Makar and Nathan MacKinnon prove costly in a 4-1 loss to the Utah Mammoth. Can the Avs’ secondary scoring step up before stars return? The first period sparks with physicality, but missing firepower leaves Colorado’s attack looking predictable and slow, despite solid efforts from Nazem Kadri and Gabriel Landeskog, who finds himself at the center of a heated scrap.

Key themes include Sebastian Cossa’s sharp goaltending for Utah, Colorado’s challenges generating high-danger chances, and the escalating rivalry marked by hard hits and a controversial fight. The episode also explores the impact of recent player injuries, special teams miscues—especially shorthanded goals allowed—and the much-anticipated reveal of the Winter Classic uniforms for both teams. videos.title: Hindi - 18.11.26 - RIFT Presentation
videos.summary_source_text:
Hindi - 18.11.26 - RIFT Presentation RIFT is a modern, non-custodial trading and financial technology ecosystem designed to bring together market access, education, intelligent execution, portfolio participation and professional trading infrastructure in one connected environment.

Built for both newcomers and experienced market participants, RIFT provides a structured journey from learning and practice through to increasingly sophisticated forms of market participation.

ONE ECOSYSTEM. MULTIPLE WAYS TO PARTICIPATE.

RIFT gives users access to a range of trading and financial tools, including:

• Demo Trading — Practice market participation using virtual capital while learning how markets, execution and platform functionality work.

• Spot Trading — Participate directly in spot markets while developing an understanding of market behaviour, patience and risk management.

• Futures Trading — Access leveraged markets with tools and functionality designed for more advanced trading strategies and risk management.

• Smart Money — Explore structured portfolio participation through features including mirror wallets and trading books, allowing users to move beyond focusing only on individual trades.

• Auto Trading Engine — Access structured automated execution through different environments designed to support systematic and repeatable participation.

• Prediction Markets — Participate in an emerging category of market infrastructure where users can trade contracts based on the probability of future events and outcomes.

• Prop Trading Infrastructure — Learn about and participate in the evolving world of proprietary trading, funded accounts, capital allocation, performance evaluation and professional risk management.

INTELLIGENT FINANCIAL INFRASTRUCTURE

RIFT is designed around the idea that the future of finance will combine human decision-making with intelligent technology.

Modern financial markets generate enormous amounts of information. Algorithms and AI systems can process data, identify patterns, monitor markets and support execution at a speed that is impossible for an individual human to replicate.

RIFT explores how these technologies can work alongside human judgement to create more structured and intelligent financial participation.

The objective is not simply to automate everything.

It is to combine people, data, technology, risk management and intelligent execution within a connected financial ecosystem.

EDUCATION AT THE CORE

RIFT places strong emphasis on education and developing a deeper understanding of financial markets.

Through the RIFT Before You Quit educational series, training sessions and community learning, participants explore subjects including:

• Trading psychology
• Risk management
• Capital preservation
• Portfolio construction
• Capital allocation
• Market structure
• Smart money concepts
• Futures and leverage
• Prediction markets
• Proprietary trading
• Behavioural finance
• Artificial intelligence
• Algorithmic execution
• Financial infrastructure
• Professional trading principles

The objective is to help participants understand not only how to participate in markets, but also why disciplined decision-making matters.

A STRUCTURED LEARNING JOURNEY

RIFT is designed to provide a progression from education and practice toward more advanced market participation:

Learn → Demo → Spot → Futures → Smart Money → Automated Execution → Professional Trading

Each stage introduces different concepts, technologies and levels of responsibility.

Rather than focusing solely on individual trades or short-term results, RIFT encourages participants to develop a broader understanding of risk, process, discipline and capital management.

NON-CUSTODIAL INFRASTRUCTURE

RIFT follows a non-custodial approach designed to give users greater control over their own funds and reduce the need to place assets into a centralized company-controlled account.

This reflects a broader movement within digital finance toward greater transparency, user control and blockchain-based infrastructure.

ACCESS FROM ANY DEVICE

RIFT is available through the web as well as its broader platform environment, making it accessible across modern computers, smartphones and other devices.

Its lightweight infrastructure is designed to make participation practical even for users with older devices, helping remove unnecessary technology barriers to accessing modern financial tools.

THE FUTURE OF FINANCIAL PARTICIPATION

Financial markets are changing rapidly.

Trading is becoming increasingly automated. Artificial intelligence is transforming data analysis. Prediction markets are creating new forms of information-based participation. Proprietary trading is expanding access to structured capital allocation models. Blockchain infrastructure is changing how digital assets can be held and transferred.

RIFT brings these developments together within one evolving ecosystem.

RIFT — THE NEXT-GEN AFFILIATE OS

Learn. Participate. Manage Risk. Think Bigger. RIFT is a modern, non-custodial trading and financial technology ecosystem designed to bring together market access, education, intelligent execution, portfolio participation and professional trading infrastructure in one connected environment.

Built for both newcomers and experienced market participants, RIFT provides a structured journey from learning and practice through to increasingly sophisticated forms of market participation.

ONE ECOSYSTEM. MULTIPLE WAYS TO PARTICIPATE.

RIFT gives users access to a range of trading and financial tools, including:

• Demo Trading — Practice market participation using virtual capital while learning how markets, execution and platform functionality work.

• Spot Trading — Participate directly in spot markets while developing an understanding of market behaviour, patience and risk management.

• Futures Trading — Access leveraged markets with tools and functionality designed for more advanced trading strategies and risk management.

• Smart Money — Explore structured portfolio participation through features including mirror wallets and trading books, allowing users to move beyond focusing only on individual trades.

• Auto Trading Engine — Access structured automated execution through different environments designed to support systematic and repeatable participation.

• Prediction Markets — Participate in an emerging category of market infrastructure where users can trade contracts based on the probability of future events and outcomes.

• Prop Trading Infrastructure — Learn about and participate in the evolving world of proprietary trading, funded accounts, capital allocation, performance evaluation and professional risk management.

INTELLIGENT FINANCIAL INFRASTRUCTURE

RIFT is designed around the idea that the future of finance will combine human decision-making with intelligent technology.

Modern financial markets generate enormous amounts of information. Algorithms and AI systems can process data, identify patterns, monitor markets and support execution at a speed that is impossible for an individual human to replicate.

RIFT explores how these technologies can work alongside human judgement to create more structured and intelligent financial participation.

The objective is not simply to automate everything.

It is to combine people, data, technology, risk management and intelligent execution within a connected financial ecosystem.

EDUCATION AT THE CORE

RIFT places strong emphasis on education and developing a deeper understanding of financial markets.

Through the RIFT Before You Quit educational series, training sessions and community learning, participants explore subjects including:

• Trading psychology
• Risk management
• Capital preservation
• Portfolio construction
• Capital allocation
• Market structure
• Smart money concepts
• Futures and leverage
• Prediction markets
• Proprietary trading
• Behavioural finance
• Artificial intelligence
• Algorithmic execution
• Financial infrastructure
• Professional trading principles

The objective is to help participants understand not only how to participate in markets, but also why disciplined decision-making matters.

A STRUCTURED LEARNING JOURNEY

RIFT is designed to provide a progression from education and practice toward more advanced market participation:

Learn → Demo → Spot → Futures → Smart Money → Automated Execution → Professional Trading

Each stage introduces different concepts, technologies and levels of responsibility.

Rather than focusing solely on individual trades or short-term results, RIFT encourages participants to develop a broader understanding of risk, process, discipline and capital management.

NON-CUSTODIAL INFRASTRUCTURE

RIFT follows a non-custodial approach designed to give users greater control over their own funds and reduce the need to place assets into a centralized company-controlled account.

This reflects a broader movement within digital finance toward greater transparency, user control and blockchain-based infrastructure.

ACCESS FROM ANY DEVICE

RIFT is available through the web as well as its broader platform environment, making it accessible across modern computers, smartphones and other devices.

Its lightweight infrastructure is designed to make participation practical even for users with older devices, helping remove unnecessary technology barriers to accessing modern financial tools.

THE FUTURE OF FINANCIAL PARTICIPATION

Financial markets are changing rapidly.

Trading is becoming increasingly automated. Artificial intelligence is transforming data analysis. Prediction markets are creating new forms of information-based participation. Proprietary trading is expanding access to structured capital allocation models. Blockchain infrastructure is changing how digital assets can be held and transferred.

RIFT brings these developments together within one evolving ecosystem.

Eat Cottage Cheese Before Bed — Here's What Happens to Your Body!  Dr. Mandell What really happens inside your body when you eat cottage cheese before bed? This simple, protein-rich food contains casein, a slow-digesting protein that gradually releases amino acids into your bloodstream throughout the night, helping support muscle protein synthesis and overnight recovery. In this video, Dr. Alan Mandell explains the fascinating physiology behind casein, why preserving muscle mass becomes increasingly important after age 40, and how adequate protein supports strength, mobility, and healthy aging. Discover how cottage cheese provides important nutrients for bone health, helps satisfy nighttime hunger, and makes a nutritious alternative to sugary evening snacks. We'll also explore the relationship between muscle mass, glucose metabolism, and maintaining your independence as you age. Sometimes the simplest foods provide powerful nutritional benefits!

Scientific Research (PubMed):

Kouw et al. (2017). "Protein Ingestion before Sleep Increases Overnight Muscle Protein Synthesis Rates in Healthy Older Men: A Randomized Controlled Trial." PMID: 28855419.

Holwerda et al. (2016). "Physical Activity Performed in the Evening Increases the Overnight Muscle Protein Synthetic Response to Presleep Protein Ingestion in Older Men." PMID: 27281811.

"Effects of Pre-Sleep Protein Consumption on Muscle-Related Outcomes: A Systematic Review" (2020). PMID: 32811763.

"Pre-Sleep Protein in Casein Supplement or Whole-Food Form Has No Impact on Resting Energy Expenditure or Hunger in Women" (2018). PMID: 30249314.

videos.title: GPT-6.2 Astra & Sol Are Here — The Demos Are Insane
videos.summary_source_text:
GPT-6.2 Astra & Sol Are Here — The Demos Are Insane OpenAI just launched GPT-6.2 Astra and GPT-6.2 Sol, skipping GPT-6.1 Astra entirely. The new flagship is 20% cheaper, supposedly beats Claude Fable 5.2 at a fraction of the cost, and has crossed OpenAI's "High" AI self-improvement threshold. But independent benchmarks tell a very different story.

Artificial Analysis scores GPT-6.2 Astra at 62, behind Claude Fable 5.2 at 65. Meanwhile, GPT-6.2 Sol delivers performance close to the previous flagship for a fraction of the cost. So is Astra really OpenAI's biggest breakthrough, or is the cheaper Sol actually the more important release?

On November 17, OpenAI introduced two new models with ambitious claims about coding, reasoning, research, engineering, cybersecurity, and cost efficiency. But once you separate OpenAI's internal benchmarks from independent testing, the picture gets much more complicated.

First, there's the showcase.

OpenAI demonstrated a playable 3D racing game called Meridian Sound Racing, reportedly generated by Astra. It also showcased a Marina City-inspired lamp designed through CAD, a Blender car simulation, an RC buggy assembly guide, financial models, and automated presentation workflows.

The racing game is publicly playable. Most of the other demonstrations aren't. OpenAI hasn't disclosed the complete prompts, failed attempts, human edits, or tool configurations behind these results. That leaves a critical question: how much of the impressive output comes from the AI model itself, and how much depends on the surrounding software and human guidance?

Then there's pricing.

GPT-6.2 Astra costs $8 per million input tokens and $40 per million output tokens, a 20% reduction from GPT-6 Astra. GPT-6.2 Sol stays at $2 input and $10 output, making Astra four times more expensive at standard token rates.

On a workload involving 10 million input tokens and 2 million output tokens per day, that's roughly $160 for Astra versus $40 for Sol. Over 30 days, the difference reaches approximately $3,600.

But cheaper tokens don't necessarily mean cheaper completed tasks.

OpenAI claims Astra beats Claude Fable 5.2 by 5.5 percentage points on Agents' Last Exam at approximately 5% of the estimated cost. Yet the comparison involves different reasoning configurations, different task counts, and estimated competitor costs.

Independent results complicate the story further. Artificial Analysis places Fable 5.2 ahead of Astra, while Epoch AI reports a tie on its broader Capabilities Index. Google's Gemini 4 Carbon also remains competitive.

And the coding results are especially interesting.

Despite OpenAI's claims about cleaner code and fewer revisions, Artificial Analysis found essentially no improvement in Astra's coding score over GPT-6 Astra. Sol's coding score actually declined on that index.

That doesn't mean the models haven't improved. It means efficiency, code quality, and correctness are different things.

The biggest practical development may actually be GPT-6.2 Sol.

Sol reaches an Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index score of 57, matching the previous GPT-6 Astra flagship. On Vals AI, Sol costs approximately $3.18 per task compared with Astra's $10.68, while their overall scores sit surprisingly close.

For developers, businesses, and anyone running AI automation at scale, that difference could matter more than another frontier-model benchmark victory.

Then there's OpenAI's most controversial claim: Astra is its first externally deployed model to reach the "High" threshold for AI self-improvement under its Preparedness framework.

Does that mean self-improving AI or AGI has arrived?

Not according to the available evidence. The threshold measures performance on internal research-engineering tasks, not autonomous self-retraining or independent recursive improvement. There's also no public independent audit confirming the result.

We also examine the missing information: unpublished context-window specifications, private legal-AI benchmarks, unverified demonstrations, hallucination rates, and the limits of current independent testing.

Ultimately, the real question isn't which model wins a carefully selected benchmark. It's which model delivers reliable, usable results at a price that makes sense.

Should you use GPT-6.2 Astra, switch to Sol, or stick with Claude Fable 5.2?

Watch the full breakdown before making that decision.

Which real-world task would you like to see Astra and Sol tested on side by side? Drop it in the comments.

Sol reaches an Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index score of 57, matching the previous GPT-6 Astra flagship. On Vals AI, Sol costs approximately $3.18 per task compared with Astra's $10.68, while their overall scores sit surprisingly close.

For developers, businesses, and anyone running AI automation at scale, that difference could matter more than another frontier-model benchmark victory.

Then there's OpenAI's most controversial claim: Astra is its first externally deployed model to reach the "High" threshold for AI self-improvement under its Preparedness framework.

Does that mean self-improving AI or AGI has arrived?

Not according to the available evidence. The threshold measures performance on internal research-engineering tasks, not autonomous self-retraining or independent recursive improvement. There's also no public independent audit confirming the result.

We also examine the missing information: unpublished context-window specifications, private legal-AI benchmarks, unverified demonstrations, hallucination rates, and the limits of current independent testing.

Ultimately, the real question isn't which model wins a carefully selected benchmark. It's which model delivers reliable, usable results at a price that makes sense.

Should you use GPT-6.2 Astra, switch to Sol, or stick with Claude Fable 5.2?

Watch the full breakdown before making that decision.

videos.title: Steroids Work - But What's Really The Problem?
videos.summary_source_text:
Steroids Work - But What's Really The Problem? Steroids build muscle. Medicine argued about it for decades, until a 1996 trial settled it. The real question was always the bill.

In this investigation: what anabolic steroids are and how they work, where they came from (Vienna 1954, Dianabol, East Germany's State Plan 14.25, Ben Johnson), who uses them today, why "steroids" is a whole family of drugs, the black-market supply chain, and what the research shows about hormones and fertility, the heart, the liver, the kidneys and the mind. Then six gym myths, and the line between supervised testosterone therapy after 40 and use without a doctor.

This is education, not a diagnosis. If you use anabolic steroids or are thinking about it, talk honestly with a doctor: blood tests and a heart check can show problems long before you feel them.

Pulls, fades, poor contact and drives that come up short often start with the left side of your body: a level setup, an all-arms backswing with no width, and a left shoulder that moves too far forward on the way down. The fix comes from what Tiger Woods, Rory McIlroy and Justin Thomas have in common: a setup with your left hip and left shoulder higher, width in the backswing, and a left shoulder that goes up and back on the downswing. Together, these golf swing tips give you the two things Eric says you need to hit driver farther, an upward angle of attack and more speed, and he shows how to adjust the downswing feel for pulls and fades or pushes and hooks. If you leave this video without trying the feel of punching the club away from you, you're leaving speed and distance on the table.

We’ll explore small movements of the pelvis, circles, and comfortable diagonal reaching, noticing how your pelvis and spine move together. Then slowly stand up and sit down again, and notice whether anything feels different.

Grab a chair, keep the movements small, and adjust them to your comfort. There’s no need to force a stretch or reach farther.

DIF-stjärnans (?!) framtid och sega starten Avsnitt 11 av Challe vs Junland – med Carl Juborg, Charles Berglund och Jonas Junland.

Djurgårdens stora frågetecken hamnar sedan i centrum: vad är egentligen rätt roll för Nils Åman – och vad händer med Noel Gunler efter petningen? Här är Challe och Junland inte överens. videos.title: 17.11.26 - RIFT Presentation
videos.summary_source_text:
17.11.26 - RIFT Presentation RIFT is a modern, non-custodial trading and financial technology ecosystem designed to bring together market access, education, intelligent execution, portfolio participation and professional trading infrastructure in one connected environment.

Built for both newcomers and experienced market participants, RIFT provides a structured journey from learning and practice through to increasingly sophisticated forms of market participation.

ONE ECOSYSTEM. MULTIPLE WAYS TO PARTICIPATE.

RIFT gives users access to a range of trading and financial tools, including:

• Demo Trading — Practice market participation using virtual capital while learning how markets, execution and platform functionality work.

• Spot Trading — Participate directly in spot markets while developing an understanding of market behaviour, patience and risk management.

• Futures Trading — Access leveraged markets with tools and functionality designed for more advanced trading strategies and risk management.

• Smart Money — Explore structured portfolio participation through features including mirror wallets and trading books, allowing users to move beyond focusing only on individual trades.

• Auto Trading Engine — Access structured automated execution through different environments designed to support systematic and repeatable participation.

• Prediction Markets — Participate in an emerging category of market infrastructure where users can trade contracts based on the probability of future events and outcomes.

• Prop Trading Infrastructure — Learn about and participate in the evolving world of proprietary trading, funded accounts, capital allocation, performance evaluation and professional risk management.

INTELLIGENT FINANCIAL INFRASTRUCTURE

RIFT is designed around the idea that the future of finance will combine human decision-making with intelligent technology.

Modern financial markets generate enormous amounts of information. Algorithms and AI systems can process data, identify patterns, monitor markets and support execution at a speed that is impossible for an individual human to replicate.

RIFT explores how these technologies can work alongside human judgement to create more structured and intelligent financial participation.

The objective is not simply to automate everything.

It is to combine people, data, technology, risk management and intelligent execution within a connected financial ecosystem.

EDUCATION AT THE CORE

RIFT places strong emphasis on education and developing a deeper understanding of financial markets.

Through the RIFT Before You Quit educational series, training sessions and community learning, participants explore subjects including:

• Trading psychology
• Risk management
• Capital preservation
• Portfolio construction
• Capital allocation
• Market structure
• Smart money concepts
• Futures and leverage
• Prediction markets
• Proprietary trading
• Behavioural finance
• Artificial intelligence
• Algorithmic execution
• Financial infrastructure
• Professional trading principles

The objective is to help participants understand not only how to participate in markets, but also why disciplined decision-making matters.

A STRUCTURED LEARNING JOURNEY

RIFT is designed to provide a progression from education and practice toward more advanced market participation:

Learn → Demo → Spot → Futures → Smart Money → Automated Execution → Professional Trading

Each stage introduces different concepts, technologies and levels of responsibility.

Rather than focusing solely on individual trades or short-term results, RIFT encourages participants to develop a broader understanding of risk, process, discipline and capital management.

NON-CUSTODIAL INFRASTRUCTURE

RIFT follows a non-custodial approach designed to give users greater control over their own funds and reduce the need to place assets into a centralized company-controlled account.

This reflects a broader movement within digital finance toward greater transparency, user control and blockchain-based infrastructure.

ACCESS FROM ANY DEVICE

RIFT is available through the web as well as its broader platform environment, making it accessible across modern computers, smartphones and other devices.

Its lightweight infrastructure is designed to make participation practical even for users with older devices, helping remove unnecessary technology barriers to accessing modern financial tools.

THE FUTURE OF FINANCIAL PARTICIPATION

Financial markets are changing rapidly.

Trading is becoming increasingly automated. Artificial intelligence is transforming data analysis. Prediction markets are creating new forms of information-based participation. Proprietary trading is expanding access to structured capital allocation models. Blockchain infrastructure is changing how digital assets can be held and transferred.

RIFT brings these developments together within one evolving ecosystem.

videos.title: Hindi - 17.11.26 - RIFT Presentation
videos.summary_source_text:
Hindi - 17.11.26 - RIFT Presentation RIFT is a modern, non-custodial trading and financial technology ecosystem designed to bring together market access, education, intelligent execution, portfolio participation and professional trading infrastructure in one connected environment.

Built for both newcomers and experienced market participants, RIFT provides a structured journey from learning and practice through to increasingly sophisticated forms of market participation.

ONE ECOSYSTEM. MULTIPLE WAYS TO PARTICIPATE.

RIFT gives users access to a range of trading and financial tools, including:

• Demo Trading — Practice market participation using virtual capital while learning how markets, execution and platform functionality work.

• Spot Trading — Participate directly in spot markets while developing an understanding of market behaviour, patience and risk management.

• Futures Trading — Access leveraged markets with tools and functionality designed for more advanced trading strategies and risk management.

• Smart Money — Explore structured portfolio participation through features including mirror wallets and trading books, allowing users to move beyond focusing only on individual trades.

• Auto Trading Engine — Access structured automated execution through different environments designed to support systematic and repeatable participation.

• Prediction Markets — Participate in an emerging category of market infrastructure where users can trade contracts based on the probability of future events and outcomes.

• Prop Trading Infrastructure — Learn about and participate in the evolving world of proprietary trading, funded accounts, capital allocation, performance evaluation and professional risk management.

INTELLIGENT FINANCIAL INFRASTRUCTURE

RIFT is designed around the idea that the future of finance will combine human decision-making with intelligent technology.

Modern financial markets generate enormous amounts of information. Algorithms and AI systems can process data, identify patterns, monitor markets and support execution at a speed that is impossible for an individual human to replicate.

RIFT explores how these technologies can work alongside human judgement to create more structured and intelligent financial participation.

The objective is not simply to automate everything.

It is to combine people, data, technology, risk management and intelligent execution within a connected financial ecosystem.

EDUCATION AT THE CORE

RIFT places strong emphasis on education and developing a deeper understanding of financial markets.

Through the RIFT Before You Quit educational series, training sessions and community learning, participants explore subjects including:

• Trading psychology
• Risk management
• Capital preservation
• Portfolio construction
• Capital allocation
• Market structure
• Smart money concepts
• Futures and leverage
• Prediction markets
• Proprietary trading
• Behavioural finance
• Artificial intelligence
• Algorithmic execution
• Financial infrastructure
• Professional trading principles

The objective is to help participants understand not only how to participate in markets, but also why disciplined decision-making matters.

A STRUCTURED LEARNING JOURNEY

RIFT is designed to provide a progression from education and practice toward more advanced market participation:

Learn → Demo → Spot → Futures → Smart Money → Automated Execution → Professional Trading

Each stage introduces different concepts, technologies and levels of responsibility.

Rather than focusing solely on individual trades or short-term results, RIFT encourages participants to develop a broader understanding of risk, process, discipline and capital management.

NON-CUSTODIAL INFRASTRUCTURE

RIFT follows a non-custodial approach designed to give users greater control over their own funds and reduce the need to place assets into a centralized company-controlled account.

This reflects a broader movement within digital finance toward greater transparency, user control and blockchain-based infrastructure.

ACCESS FROM ANY DEVICE

RIFT is available through the web as well as its broader platform environment, making it accessible across modern computers, smartphones and other devices.

Its lightweight infrastructure is designed to make participation practical even for users with older devices, helping remove unnecessary technology barriers to accessing modern financial tools.

THE FUTURE OF FINANCIAL PARTICIPATION

Financial markets are changing rapidly.

Trading is becoming increasingly automated. Artificial intelligence is transforming data analysis. Prediction markets are creating new forms of information-based participation. Proprietary trading is expanding access to structured capital allocation models. Blockchain infrastructure is changing how digital assets can be held and transferred.

RIFT brings these developments together within one evolving ecosystem.

videos.title: Please STOP Gripping Your Dumbbells Like This!
videos.summary_source_text:
Please STOP Gripping Your Dumbbells Like This! Your wrists shouldn’t be the reason you cut your chest workout short. If you get wrist pain when doing a dumbbell bench press, take a look at how you’re gripping the weight.

The problem? Grabbing the dumbbell right in the middle and letting the thumb side of your hand drop can put your wrist in an uncomfortable position under load. Before you pick up another set, try making this small adjustment.

The fix is simple:
Shift your grip slightly toward the end of the handle and focus your squeeze through your ring and pinky fingers. This helps position the pinky side of your hand slightly higher than the thumb side.

In this video, I’ll show you why that small change matters using the bones of the wrist and forearm. Adjusting the angle of your hand changes how the weight loads the wrist and can help make your dumbbell pressing more comfortable.

Same exercise. Better grip.

videos.title: xAI's Grok 5 Is INSANE: Elon Musk's Plan to Reach AGI!
videos.summary_source_text:
xAI's Grok 5 Is INSANE: Elon Musk's Plan to Reach AGI! Elon Musk says Grok 5 has a 10% chance of becoming AGI and could be the smartest AI in the world across every metric. But there's one major problem: Grok 5 still hasn't launched, and none of those predictions comes with independently verified benchmarks.

Behind the hype is a massive AI infrastructure project: xAI's Colossus supercomputer in Memphis, reportedly approaching 440,000 GPUs, gigawatt-scale power requirements, and a federal legal battle over gas turbines. Musk has also reportedly discussed a six-trillion-parameter model capable of real-time video understanding and advanced autonomous agents.

But can more computing power actually deliver artificial general intelligence? And why do Grok 5's release deadlines keep slipping?

We trace five major Grok 5 promises, from Musk's September 2025 AGI prediction and 10% probability estimate to the shifting launch timeline that now places Grok 4.8 and Grok 4.9 ahead of Grok 5.

Then we examine what xAI has actually delivered. Grok 4.7 posted improvements in coding benchmarks, including 71.0% on DeepSWE 1.1, 46.3% on CursorBench 4.0, and 37.6% on Terminal-Bench 4.0 according to xAI. With pricing starting at $2 per million input tokens and $6 per million output tokens, Grok has a compelling cost advantage.

However, independent comparisons tell a more complicated story. Grok 4.7 trails leading models from OpenAI and Anthropic on several evaluations, while Google's Gemini 4 Argon raises the competitive bar even further. We examine GPT-6 Astra, GPT-6.1 Sol, Claude Fable 5.1, Claude Opus 5.5, and the benchmark differences that marketing headlines often overlook.

And there's a revealing twist: shortly before Grok 4.7 launched, Musk himself suggested it would be closer to an older Claude Opus model, while positioning Grok 4.9 as the potential competitor to newer frontier systems. That puts his extraordinary Grok 5 predictions into perspective.

We also investigate Colossus 2, reports of a possible 1.1-million-GPU expansion, the NAACP's environmental challenge, and the Justice Department's national-security argument. Plus, we separate existing Grok Imagine, Grok Voice, and Grok Build capabilities from the much harder promises of unified real-time video reasoning and long-running autonomous agents.

Finally, we examine the AGI question itself. What would Grok 5 need to demonstrate on independent tests like ARC-AGI and Humanity's Last Exam? Can it handle multi-day projects without supervision? And how would xAI address safety, misinformation, and adversarial content risks inherited from earlier Grok releases?

Three outcomes remain possible: a genuine breakthrough, a strong but incremental frontier model, or another release that falls short of enormous expectations.

The real test won't be Musk's next prediction. It will be what independent evaluators discover after Grok 5 actually ships.

Subscribe to BitBiased for independent AI analysis, benchmark comparisons, and the technology stories behind the headlines.

videos.summary_source_text:
Every Shot Of Jon Rahm's Final Winning Round | 2026 Abu Dhabi Aldar Championship Every shot from Jon Rahm's final round at the 2026 Abu Dhabi Aldar Championship where he secured his record winning SIXTH Rolex Series victory on the DP World Tour, taking down Tyrrell Hatton and Rory McIlroy.

► SUBSCRIBE: http://et.golf/Subscribe 

After 40 events, five global swings, the Back 9 and four Majors, the DP World Tour Play-Offs are upon us. The top 70 available players from the Race to Dubai Rankings Delivered by DP World tee it up this week at Yas Links before the top 50 then move on to the season-finale at the DP World Tour Championship. Both those events form part of the Rolex Series, with Patrick Reed, Tom Kim and JJ Spaun having already been crowned Rolex Series champions in 2026. With full playing privileges on the DP World Tour now secured the focus turns to the quest to be Europe’s Number One and claim the Harry Vardon Trophy. Rory McIlroy is looking to equal Colin Montgomerie's record of eight season-long wins with his fifth in a row but the Northern Irishman is in the unusual position of being the hunter rather than the hunted. Last year, Aaron Rai beat fellow Englishman Tommy Fleetwood in a play-off to win his second Rolex Series title at Yas Links, five years on from his first at the Scottish Open. The 70 player field is stacked with star-studded names, featuring 6 major winners including Rory McIlroy, Jon Rahm and Patrick Reed alongside three-time season winner Eugenio Chacarra who will be hoping to add a Rolex Series title to his CV. With enhanced points on offer it also means that the jostling for dual membership with the PGA Tour is far from over.

videos.title: Where is Jensen Huang's Girlfriend?!
videos.summary_source_text:
Where is Jensen Huang's Girlfriend?! Who is Alice Huang, the woman at the center of the alleged Chinese espionage scandal involving NVIDIA and Jensen Huang? From her early career in Chinese television and finance to her reported relationship with NVIDIA's CEO and her current whereabouts, this documentary investigates everything we know about Alice Huang.

Alice Huang, also known as Huang Le, has become one of the most controversial figures in the NVIDIA story. US officials reportedly suspect her of having connections to Chinese intelligence. But how much of the story is supported by evidence, and how much remains unverified?

In this documentary, we investigate Alice Huang's biography, her reported work at CCTV, HSBC, and CITIC Securities, her connection to Megaspeed International, and how she entered Jensen Huang's professional circle.

We also examine the reported affair involving Jensen Huang, his resignation, NVIDIA's response, the Singapore investigation, Taiwan's restrictions, and reports that Alice Huang is now living in Beijing.

Most importantly, we separate documented facts from intelligence allegations and unanswered questions.

**In this video:**
- Who is Alice Huang, also known as Huang Le?
- Her early life, career, and financial background
- How Megaspeed International connected her to NVIDIA
- How she reportedly met Jensen Huang
- The relationship and alleged Chinese intelligence connection
- What US officials have claimed about espionage
- What Singapore's investigation actually established
- Why Jensen Huang resigned from NVIDIA
- Where Alice Huang is reportedly living today
- What remains unknown about the alleged spy scandal
