The publicly available evidence does not establish that she was. This investigation examines what authorities have confirmed, what major news organizations have reported, and what remains unproven.

**Sources referenced:** Reuters, Bloomberg, Associated Press, The New York Times, Financial Times, The Wall Street Journal, Singapore Ministry of Home Affairs, Taiwan authorities, and NVIDIA regulatory filings.

It’s time for an Audi vs Audi head-to-head! 

We’ve got our hands on the all-new Audi RS5, and it’s lining up against the almighty Audi RS6 GT! 

The RS5 may be the newest car here, but it has one key difference to the RS6 GT - it’s powered by a V6 hybrid system, while the RS6 GT is packing a twin-turbo V8! But which will come out on top? Let’s take a closer look at the stats…

This power is sent to all four wheels via an 8-speed auto gearbox, and it’s significantly heavier than the RS6, tipping the scales at 2,355kg! It may be the newer car, but it’s notably cheaper than the RS6 GT, coming in at £89,400.

videos.title: 16.11.26 - Ep.26 (Part 7) - The Prop Trading Shift
videos.summary_source_text:
16.11.26 - Ep.26 (Part 7) - The Prop Trading Shift In Part 7 of Episode 26, we move from traditional order-book trading into the world of decentralised market structure. Having explored execution awareness, liquidity, slippage, market impact and exit strategies, we now examine how decentralised exchanges organise liquidity and determine prices.

We compare central limit order books (CLOBs) with automated market makers (AMMs), exploring how liquidity pools work, how mathematical pricing curves affect execution, and why the size of a trade matters relative to the available liquidity.

The session also introduces liquidity providers, impermanent loss, concentrated liquidity and arbitrage, explaining the opportunities and risks involved in providing liquidity to decentralised markets.

What You Will Learn

1. Central Limit Order Books vs Automated Market Makers

Why decentralised exchanges do not necessarily rely on liquidity pools.

How central limit order books match individual buy and sell orders.

How automated market makers use pooled assets and mathematical pricing.

The difference between individual orders and liquidity reserves.

Why Hyperliquid is an example of an on-chain order-book trading architecture.

2. How Automated Market Makers Work

Understanding liquidity pools containing two different assets, such as ETH and USDC.

How traders swap against the reserves held in a smart contract.

The role of liquidity providers in supplying assets to pools.

Understanding the constant product formula: x × y = k.

How changes in pool reserves affect the price of an asset.

3. Trade Size and Price Impact

Why buying larger quantities from the same pool results in progressively higher execution prices.

Practical examples using pools containing ETH and USDC.

Why a trade's size must be considered relative to available liquidity.

How deeper liquidity pools reduce the price impact of individual trades.

Why the mathematical pricing curve determines the cost of additional trade volume.

4. Price Impact vs Slippage

Understanding the difference between price impact and slippage.

How your own order changes the pricing conditions within a liquidity pool.

How other transactions occurring before yours can change the final execution price.

Why even a deep liquidity pool cannot eliminate slippage during rapid market movements.

5. Arbitrage and Price Alignment

Why the price inside an AMM pool can differ from prices on other exchanges.

How arbitrage traders exploit price differences between markets.

How buying and selling activity helps bring prices back into alignment.

Why arbitrage is not risk-free, with trading fees, gas costs, latency and execution risk all affecting profitability.

6. Liquidity Providers and Impermanent Loss

How liquidity providers deposit assets into smart contract pools.

How trading fees are distributed according to each provider's contribution.

Why liquidity provision is a form of market making rather than risk-free income.

Understanding impermanent loss and divergence loss.

How changes in asset prices affect the composition of a liquidity provider's holdings.

Why trading fees may offset some or all of the difference compared with simply holding the assets.

7. Full-Range vs Concentrated Liquidity

Why traditional full-range liquidity can be capital inefficient.

How Uniswap V3 introduced concentrated liquidity.

How liquidity providers can select specific price ranges for their capital.

Why concentrated liquidity can improve capital efficiency.

The risks of price moving outside a selected range, making liquidity inactive.

Understanding ticks and how liquidity becomes active or inactive as prices move.

8. Concentrated Liquidity and Range Orders

How narrow liquidity ranges can behave similarly to limit orders.

Why concentrated liquidity is not identical to a traditional limit order.

How price reversals can affect a liquidity provider's position.

Why understanding the mechanics is essential before providing liquidity.

Understanding the Architecture Behind Decentralised Trading

This session introduces two fundamentally different ways of organising market liquidity.

With an order book, liquidity is displayed through individual orders at specific prices. With an automated market maker, liquidity is held in pools and prices are determined by mathematical formulas.

Both approaches solve the same underlying problem: how buyers and sellers access executable liquidity.

Understanding these differences is particularly important as we develop our trading strategies and explore the wider decentralised trading ecosystem.

Understand the market beyond the charts. Learn how liquidity works. Build your trading knowledge from the ground up. videos.title: Qwen4 Max Just Dropped, China's New BEST AI Model!
videos.summary_source_text:
Qwen4 Max Just Dropped, China's New BEST AI Model! Alibaba just launched Qwen4-Max, a 2.4 trillion parameter AI now ranked China's best on Arena. It claims major coding gains, cuts task costs by over 60%, and even spends 48 hours designing a real coolant molecule that robots produce. videos.title: Eldrivna BMW M3 provkörd – jag körde originalet för 40 år sedan
videos.summary_source_text:
Eldrivna BMW M3 provkörd – jag körde originalet för 40 år sedan Läs hela testet på: https://alriksbilar.se/artiklar/bmw-m3-elektrisk/

För 40 år sedan var jag nyanställd på Teknikens Värld och skickades till Italien för att köra en väldigt speciell bil. Första BMW M3. 200 hästar, 1 200 kilo och sjukt kul.

Nu står jag på BMW:s testbana i Miramas med sjunde generationen. Den är eldriven. Fyra elmotorer, en per hjul. Batteri på 100 kWh, 420 kW snabbladdning och runt 650 kilometers räckvidd. Vikten? Den vill ingen på BMW säga ett ord om …

Jag åker först med Klaus Huber, chef för Driving Dynamics på BMW M. Sedan kör jag själv. Tre pass, det sista i regn. Jag testar låtsasväxlarna som BMW kallar stages, ljudet, sladdlägena och hur mycket bil man egentligen kan ställa om med några knapptryck. Johannes Bauer och Johannes Jurran förklarar tekniken bakom.

Så frågan. Är det här en äkta M3? Jag har kört alla generationer och jag har ett svar. Men vad tycker du? Skulle du ta den eldrivna eller vänta på bensinversionen? Skriv i kommentarerna!

Bilen är en kamouflerad prototyp, så allt är inte färdigt än.

videos.title: Gemini 4 KRYPTON Is INSANE — It Just Coded an Entire Game!
videos.summary_source_text:
Gemini 4 KRYPTON Is INSANE — It Just Coded an Entire Game! Google's rumored Gemini 4 Krypton has sparked a massive question: did an unreleased AI model just prove it can build entire games? A leaked demo reportedly shows an eight-second anime-style animation generated entirely through code, taking 39 minutes and potentially involving nearly 247,000 tokens. But there's a major difference between generating impressive visuals and creating a playable game.

And that's where this story gets interesting.

On November 8, an X user known as Lyra claimed Google had developed an internal checkpoint called Krypton, reportedly outperforming Gemini 4 Carbon. Another developer, Chetaslua, shared comparisons involving a model labeled "krypton-a," including a detailed PlayStation 4 controller rendered in SVG and an anime-style floating island animation.

The numbers are striking. According to the reported comparison, Krypton used approximately 22,000 thinking tokens to generate the controller, versus 4,000 for Carbon. The anime animation reportedly ran for 39 minutes and 16 seconds at roughly 105 tokens per second.

But none of this has been independently verified. Google hasn't officially announced Gemini 4 Krypton, published its benchmarks, confirmed its specifications, or provided a release date.

So what can these leaked demonstrations actually tell us?

We examine the origins of the Krypton name, the reported visual comparisons, the quarter-million-token calculation, and why producing an animation isn't equivalent to building an interactive game with player controls, collision detection, physics, and functioning gameplay systems.

Then we compare those rumors with something Google has already demonstrated: four Gemini 4 Argon AI agents working together inside Minecraft.

According to published research, the agents defeated the Ender Dragon in 27 hours and 14 minutes, writing 2,783 programs and dying 605 times along the way. Unlike a short visual demo, this experiment involved extended planning, execution, failure, and recovery. But the agents were playing Minecraft through a programming interface, not building the game itself.

Google's official AI lineup makes the story even more interesting.

Gemini 4 Carbon, announced October 28 and expanded to more users November 10, focuses on difficult, long-horizon reasoning, software engineering, debugging, and complex workflows.

Gemini 4 Hydrogen, officially introduced November 12, takes a different approach: faster coding and agentic execution. Google lists a one-million-token unified context window and pricing of $1.50 per million input tokens and $7.50 per million output tokens.

Alongside Hydrogen, Google introduced Orchestrator in Antigravity, allowing different models to handle different parts of a development workflow. Google reports that Orchestrator achieved task success close to Carbon while using 24% less quota and finishing 19% faster on average on Terminal-Bench 4.0.

But how does Google's AI actually compare against OpenAI and Anthropic?

We examine the reported benchmark results, including Carbon's Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index score of 59, compared with Claude Opus 5.5 at 58 and GPT-6 Astra at 57.

The competition becomes more complicated on coding benchmarks. Carbon reportedly scores 61.2% on FrontierSWE 2, behind GPT-6 Astra's 65.5%, while leading on the cited Terminal-Bench 4.0 comparison with 65.2%.

These are different evaluations measuring different capabilities. None proves an AI can independently produce a polished, enjoyable game.

We also explore what OpenAI Codex, Anthropic's coding agents, and xAI's Grok game-generation demonstrations reveal about the growing competition in AI-assisted software development.

For game developers, the bigger question isn't whether AI can generate thousands of lines of code. It's whether AI agents can build, test, debug, and improve working interactive experiences reliably.

So did Gemini 4 Krypton actually build a game? Is Google testing a breakthrough coding model, or are viral demos creating expectations that the evidence doesn't support?

The distinction matters more than ever.

A leaked demo reportedly shows an eight-second anime-style animation generated entirely through code, taking 39 minutes and potentially involving nearly 247,000 tokens. But there's a major difference between generating impressive visuals and creating a playable game.

And that's where this story gets interesting.

On November 8, an X user known as Lyra claimed Google had developed an internal checkpoint called Krypton, reportedly outperforming Gemini 4 Carbon. Another developer, Chetaslua, shared comparisons involving a model labeled "krypton-a," including a detailed PlayStation 4 controller rendered in SVG and an anime-style floating island animation.

The numbers are striking. According to the reported comparison, Krypton used approximately 22,000 thinking tokens to generate the controller, versus 4,000 for Carbon. The anime animation reportedly ran for 39 minutes and 16 seconds at roughly 105 tokens per second.

Grip strength predicts the risk of dying better than blood pressure, yet fewer than 1 in 3 adults do the one thing that brings muscle back.

Education, not a diagnosis. Talk to your doctor before starting a new training program.

videos.summary_source_text:
This Fixes 95% of Posture Problems (FAST!) If you want to learn how to fix bad posture in 22 days, this step by step video gives you a plan for improving posture with stretches and strengthening exercises. Instead of guessing which posture exercises you need, I’m going to show you six simple tests you can perform at home to identify areas that need attention. Then, I’ll show you the stretches and exercises to address them and build your own posture correction routine.

Workouts, supplements, and mealplans here - http://athleanx.com
Subscribe to this channel here - http://youtube.com/user/jdcav24

The key to better posture is addressing your specific limitations consistently. This 22 day posture routine starts with testing your movement so you can focus on the areas that need work.

How to fix bad posture:

Day one starts with the posture test. As a physical therapist, I recommend seeing a qualified professional for an individual evaluation to understand your posture, the severity of any limitations and differences between your left and right sides. The six tests in this video give you a starting point for identifying areas to work on at home.

We’re looking at six areas: thoracic spine mobility, hamstring flexibility, calf flexibility, abdominal flexibility, hip flexor mobility and hip rotation. A rounded upper back, tight hamstrings, tight calves, tight abs, tight hip flexors and limited hip rotation can all affect how you move. Testing each area helps you decide which mobility exercises and stretches belong in your routine.

Each test uses a pass or fail approach. If you pass a test, you can skip the corresponding correction in this plan. If you fail a test, include the stretches and strengthening exercises shown for that area. This keeps your posture workout focused on your results instead of having you perform every exercise whether you need it or not.

After your initial assessment, alternate stretching days with exercise or strengthening days for the next 20 days. Follow the recommended hold times, sets and reps demonstrated in the video for each of your selected corrections. On day 22, repeat the original tests to see where your mobility and control have improved and what still needs attention.

For example, if your upper back is rounded and you struggle to extend through your thoracic spine, start with the kneeling thoracic extension stretch. Place your elbows on a surface in front of you, lower your chest and gently move your upper back into extension. The goal is to work on upper back mobility with control rather than force yourself into a position you cannot comfortably reach.

On your strengthening days, the face pull works the muscles of the upper back and shoulders. When you’re looking for exercises for rounded shoulders or ways to improve upper body posture, it’s easy to focus only on stretching. This routine pairs mobility work with strengthening so you also train the muscles that help you control your position.

The same approach applies to the other areas you test. Tight hip flexors, limited hip rotation or tight hamstrings may call for different corrections, which is why the assessment comes first. Use the demonstrations to choose your exercises for bad posture, and follow the instructions instead of adding random stretches to your day.

Improving posture takes consistency. You didn’t develop your everyday movement habits in a single day, and one posture stretch is not going to change everything overnight. Treat these 22 days as an opportunity to establish a repeatable routine, measure your progress and learn which areas deserve more attention.

You also don’t want to overdo the stretching. More force does not automatically mean better flexibility. Stay within a comfortable range, use controlled movement and avoid pushing through pain. The goal of these stretches for better posture is to gradually improve the movement you have available, not turn each session into a test of how much discomfort you can tolerate.

A useful posture correction routine combines flexibility, joint mobility and strength. Stretching addresses the restrictions identified by your tests, while the strengthening days help you practice controlling your movement. Keep following the schedule and use your final assessment to guide what you continue working on beyond day 22.

If you want to support better posture over the long term, complement this routine with a workout program that strengthens your entire body. The ATHLEAN-X programs combine strength training with attention to how you move. Head to athleanx.com and use the program selector to find the training plan that fits your goals.

For more videos on how to improve posture, stretches for tight muscles, upper back exercises and full body strength training, subscribe to the ATHLEAN-X YouTube channel.
